findings.passage: a nearly 45-minute parody she directed and starred in as Katniss
findings.problem: The runtime is overstated in the body, the parody FAQ ('A nearly 45-minute parody') and the Nine paragraph ('a nearly 45-minute parody'). YouTube lists the parody at 2,533 seconds (42:13), checked 2026-10-16; the Leader-Telegram (S05) and Milwaukee Magazine (S14) say 42 minutes, while the NYT copy (S09) says 'nearly 45-minute'. The figure is the Times' rounding, stated as fact.
findings.acceptance_test: Every runtime mention says 42 minutes (or 'about 42-minute'), or explicitly attributes 'nearly 45-minute' to the Times. C09, C52 and C104 record the YouTube runtime and the date checked.

findings.passage: told her that when she described the parody in rehearsals, "you were really underplaying it." Then he praised her directing.
findings.problem: In S39 the captions are unlabeled from 0:40:17 to 0:41:42, and Soresi's co-host Russell is present. Russell also worked on Ginger Twinsies (S39 0:10:25; S06 cites a BroadwayWorld cast item naming Russell Daniels). Those lines include the 'underplaying' remark, the directing praise ('we never even believed in ourselves enough to direct it' suggests two hosts) and the Psycho comparison. The article gives all three to Soresi ('told her', 'he praised', 'he contrasted') without speaker confirmation. Her own lines (credit to the source film, the apology, 'I'll take it') are clearly hers.
findings.acceptance_test: Either an audio check confirms Soresi as the speaker of each of the three lines, recorded in C64/C120, or the passage attributes them to the hosts of The Downside (for example 'Soresi and his co-host, both Ginger Twinsies castmates') without naming a single speaker. Her quoted lines and the acceptance beat stay.

findings.passage: She fears a swollen ego and, she told Soresi, brought her therapist "a list of like all like the mistakes I made today."
findings.problem: This is the one Soresi reference that does not say which of the three Soresi conversations it comes from (it is S39, The Downside, February 2026). unfamiliar-04's acceptance test required every Soresi reference to do so, and the resolution claims they all do.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence names the conversation (for example 'she told Soresi on The Downside in February 2026'), and every other Soresi mention still does.

findings.passage: Some outlets say she was born in Chippewa Falls, but her father told the Leader-Telegram the family was living in Madison when she was born.
findings.problem: S05 states the Madison birth in its own narration ('They moved to Madison, where Grace Reiter was born'), not in a quote from Tim Reiter. The FAQ attributes reporting to the father. Her own account (S18 00:06:57, 2022: 'born in Verona, just a little south of Madison') is the stronger source and goes unused.
findings.acceptance_test: The FAQ attributes the Madison-area birth to the Leader-Telegram's reporting and/or her own 2022 statement, not to her father, and C48 is updated to match. Do not add an unsupported birthplace field.

findings.passage: strangers on the street shouted [Jennifer Lawrence](/personality-analysis/jennifer-lawrence)'s name at her and called her Katniss
findings.problem: The source says 'I walked on the street, people go Jennifer Lawrence, Hunger Games' (S42 0:08:48). 'Shouted' and 'strangers' add volume and specificity she did not state.
findings.acceptance_test: The paraphrase uses only what the source supports, for example 'people on the street said Jennifer Lawrence's name to her and called her Katniss'. The quoted 'which I guess was kind of always my dream' is unchanged.

findings.passage: Reiter leaned in: "actually, you know what? Yes. No, we're doing it." She would, she said, "start faking it until I make it."
findings.problem: In S47 (1:27:58-1:28:38) the mock self-praise and the faking-it vow are about her personal appeal: the bit continues with funny men 'pulling' partners. They are not about her comedy or its reception. The next paragraph pivots to 'applause' and 'what she does with the applause once it stops stinging', so readers may take the vow as being about praise for her work.
findings.acceptance_test: Without quoting romantic wording, the closing makes clear in a few neutral words that the bit concerned her appeal rather than her work (for example 'mock self-praise about her own appeal'). Alternatively, the final paragraph presents the applause question as a separate forward test, not as what the vow was about.
